title: Fix the art-processing steps so they no longer change the artwork's red colour by one value
tier_reason: Four palette colours read as lost from the build when they are present one red step off, so the art scoreboard is reporting drift that has not happened.
ask: Landed without Daniel: “Confirm the four visual treatments worth rendering for Daniel to choose between”. Four palette colours read as lost from the build when they are present one red step off, so the art scoreboard is reporting drift that has not happened.
first_action: Find the step between generation and the shipped PNG that turns d2e077 into d1e077, and re-run the four affected sheets through it once fixed
source_message: Landed without Daniel: “Confirm the four visual treatments worth rendering for Daniel to choose between”.
result: The proposed processing fault was disproved before changing the sprites. The archived hillside raw and shipped PNG have the same SHA-256; both contain #d1e077 and neither contains #d2e077. The generator supplied the one-step variant. The other absent guide colours, #c49a6c and #aa7959, have #c39a6c and #a97959 as explicit locks in later asset recipes. There is no responsible downstream processing step or set of four sheets to rerun, so the artwork and raw provenance stay intact. HQ now decodes the RGB hillside and reports 53 shipped sheets, 13 exact guide colours and three one-red-step matches, with no decode failures. The art guide records the corrected finding. The focused palette tests passed, and GitHub Actions run 35970737989 passed writing, gateway and game tests. No independent checker or Daniel art acceptance was recorded.
